title: Redwood Private VPC Security Architecture Deep Dive - Latchford Trust
summary: Deep dive on Private/VPC deployment security architecture. Covered network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling (SGs/NACLs), transit patterns, private endpoints, data residency, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO evidence flow, RBAC/SSO and audit log retention. Agreed next steps: share detailed network diagram, SOC 2 report, proposed firewall rule set, and schedule POC bench in Redwood Private staging VPC.
topics: Network isolation and segmentation (VPCs, subnets, AZ placement)
Ingress patterns (ALB, private endpoints, reverse proxy, TLS termination)
Egress controls and NAT vs egress-only gateways
Security groups vs NACLs and recommended rule hygiene
Transit patterns (Transit Gateway, VPC peering) and cross-account routing
Bastion/jump hosts, Admin access and Session manager alternatives
KMS integration, HSM, encryption at rest and in transit
RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta), provisioning and SCIM sync
SOC2/ISO evidence flow and customer-managed control points
On-prem / air-gapped considerations and VPN/direct connect
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Evan Roberts (Latchford), Priya Khanna (Latchford CISO), Mark Chen (Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Legal)

---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intro  i'm Maya, i'll be your AE. Jordan will take the deep tech questions. Evan, Priya, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Evan: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. we're hoping to validate network and compliance posture for a Private/VPC deployment. primary concerns: isolation, ingress/egress controls, auditability.
[00:24] Jordan: Great. i'll run through our typical private topology, then we can map it to your controls. i'll call out where you retain control vs where Redwood manages things.
[00:37] Priya: also need to understand SOC 2 evidence and KMS options  whether we can keep keys in our HSM.
[00:45] Jordan: absolutely, we'll cover KMS/HSM, encryption, and audit log flows.

[02:15] Jordan: high level: Redwood Private runs a customer-dedicated control plane in our managed service, but for your VPC deployment we provision a set of worker subnets inside your account or a customer-managed project. all inference hosts sit in private subnets with no public ip's. we use private endpoints for control-plane traffic.
[02:38] Mark: when you say "private endpoints" do you mean AWS interface endpoints or some kind of ALB in front?
[02:44] Jordan: good question. we can do either. common pattern is interface VPC endpoints for S3 and control-plane traffic plus a private NLB/ALB in front of the inference autoscaling group  but the ALB is internal-only (no public internet). TLS terminates at the ALB or can be end-to-end to the host if you require mTLS.
[03:10] Evan: mTLS would be required for us on sensitive paths. we have strict egress firewall rules.
[03:16] Jordan: we support mutual TLS and client cert pinning. alternatively we can put the inference hosts behind a private ALB and require client auth at edge.

[05:00] Maya: i want to pause on network isolation. Jordan, walk through segmentation and how we prevent cross-tenant bleed.
[05:10] Jordan: sure. isolation is enforced at multiple layers: separate VPCs per customer or separate subnets with strict security group rules; processes run in tenant-scoped containers/VMs; data volumes are customer-scoped and encrypted with KMS keys per-customer. for shared-host models we enforce process isolation and filesystem-level encryption, but for your case we recommend dedicated hosts.
[05:45] Priya: dedicated hosts is our preference. also curious about AZ placement  do you span multiple AZs for HA and does that affect our network policy?
[05:55] Jordan: we do multi-AZ for HA. each AZ gets dedicated subnets. we recommend your NACLs be permissive for internal CIDR ranges we provide and restrictive otherwise. security groups are the primary micro-segmentation control.
[06:20] Mark: what's the recommended SG baseline?
[06:24] Jordan: least privilege: allow inbound from load balancer subnets on application ports only, allow control-plane management from the management CIDR (your admin jump box), and limit outbound to required services (S3 endpoint, KMS endpoints, telemetry). avoid wide 0.0.0.0/0 rules.

[08:00] Evan: ingress  we have an internal API gateway. can Redwood integrate with our gateway or do you need to expose endpoints?
[08:12] Jordan: you can front Redwood with your gateway. typical pattern: your API gateway calls the internal ALB endpoint. we also support VPC peering or Transit Gateway setups if you prefer centralized routing.
[08:30] Priya: about egress  we block all egress except to a few whitelisted destinations. how does Redwood handle outbound dependencies (metrics, model pull, updates)?
[08:42] Jordan: we support two modes: outbound via your NAT/egress gateway where you control allowed destinations, or we can host an egress proxy in your account which funnels traffic through approved endpoints. model artifacts can be pulled from a private S3 with VPC endpoint. telemetry can be sent to your telemetry endpoint via a private endpoint or forwarded to your SIEM via a VPC peered collector.
[09:10] Mark: so no need for internet-facing egress for model downloads if we host artifacts in our S3?
[09:14] Jordan: correct  private S3 endpoint + IAM role access handles it.

[11:00] Jordan: next, firewalling and rule hygiene. security groups are stateful and should be used for host-level access; NACLs can provide subnet-level stateless filters for defense in depth. we recommend deny-all NACL with explicit allow for necessary ports between subnets.
[11:20] Jordan: also we advise to log NACL denies at the VPC flow log level and ship flow logs to your SIEM for forensic analysis.
[11:33] Priya: what about port exposure for admin access? we prefer Session Manager over bastions.
[11:38] Jordan: we support SSM session manager for host admin  no SSH port required. for privileged sessions we can integrate with your SSO and record session transcripts.

[13:45] Evan: data residency  our customers require that data never leaves EU. we have an EU account and want the entire stack in eu-west-1. is that supported?
[13:55] Jordan: yes. Redwood supports region-restricted deployments and we can provision private infra in your EU account or in a Redwood-managed region dedicated to you with contractual data residency guarantees.
[14:10] Priya: and backups / logs  do those transit outside region?
[14:15] Jordan: backups and audit logs can remain in-region. if you use our managed observability we can ensure logs are stored in region, or you can forward to your in-region SIEM via private peering.

[16:00] Maya: timebox on encryption: KMS and HSM questions from Priya.
[16:08] Priya: yes, we need to bring our own keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys for certain data classes.
[16:15] Jordan: we support BYOK via AWS KMS external key material or customer-managed KMS keys in your account. for the highest assurance we can integrate with your HSM using CloudHSM and keep the customer master key in your account. Redwood uses envelope encryption  data keys are generated and encrypted with your CMK. logs containing sensitive PII can be redacted before leaving hosts.
[16:42] Priya: is there any part of the encryption key lifecycle Redwood controls?
[16:47] Jordan: for customer-managed keys you retain control of key rotation and deletion. Redwood only gets encrypted data keys when needed to decrypt in-host. if you revoke access to the CMK we cannot decrypt future data.

[18:30] Mark: audit logs: what do you capture and how long do you retain? we need at least seven years for some records.
[18:38] Jordan: we capture API calls, control-plane operations, model inference request metadata (no request payload by default unless you opt in), host-level logs, and VPC flow logs. retention is configurable  we can forward to your long-term storage (S3 Glacier) or keep in our managed logs with retention policies. seven years is supported via export.
[19:05] Sofia: legal question  can we get a signed SOC 2 report and do you allow customer audit?
[19:12] Maya: yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts under an NDA. customer audit access is negotiable; many customers do a security questionnaire and we provide evidence and a SOC 2 bridge letter.
[19:30] Priya: do you provide system logs that map user actions to identities (SSO)?
[19:36] Jordan: yes, we emit user-identity mapping for management plane events via SSO. we support SAML Okta, Azure AD, and SCIM provisioning.

[21:00] Evan: network egress  what about egress filtering for telemetry? we want telemetry only to our datadog endpoint.
[21:12] Jordan: we can configure telemetry to point to your Datadog intake via private peering or VPC endpoint; otherwise it goes to Redwood telemetry which you can opt out of. we can also provide a signed contract for data usage.

[23:00] Maya: let's talk about transit patterns for multi-account setups. Jordan?
[23:08] Jordan: two common patterns: Transit Gateway with central routing and TGW attachments from customer accounts, or VPC peering for one-to-one. TGW scales better and centralizes egress auditor controls. we can support route tables that only allow specific CIDR ranges to talk to the Redwood subnets.
[23:40] Mark: any concerns with asymmetric routing?
[23:44] Jordan: we recommend symmetric routing via TGW and avoid NAT hairpinning. also use source/destination checks as appropriate and maintain route table hygiene.

[25:30] Priya: compliance controls  how do we get evidence for SOC2?
[25:36] Jordan: Redwood provides an evidence portal where you can pull audit artifacts, config snapshots, and logs. for private deployments we can give scoped evidence showing config in your VPC plus Redwood's operational logs.
[26:00] Maya: we'll share the SOC 2 package after the call; Jordan will annotate where customer controls are required.

[28:10] Evan: for POC staging, can you spin up a small cluster in our staging account so we can run a perf benchmark through our firewall rules?
[28:20] Jordan: yes  we typically do a 1-2 week bench in a staging VPC. requires IAM role creation and a small peered endpoint; we can work with your infra to limit permissions.
[28:32] Mark: what are the minimum ports for the bench?
[28:35] Jordan: app ports plus control-plane on 443 and egress to S3 endpoint for artifacts. we'll provide a one-page firewall checklist.

[31:00] Priya: question on RBAC  how do you map Redwood roles to our SSO identities and audit role changes?
[31:08] Jordan: we support SSO SAML integration and SCIM for provisioning. role mappings are configurable and changes are logged. we also support enforced MFA and role-based session timeouts.
[31:32] Evan: can we restrict which users can call model-run APIs vs admin APIs?
[31:36] Jordan: yes  we have token scopes and route-level RBAC. tokens can be minted by your identity provider and scoped.

[34:00] Maya: some quick imperfect transcriptions  you might see "KV cash" in the notes  that's KV cache.
[34:08] Evan: (laughs) yes we've seen that in other calls.

[36:00] Jordan: about firewalling between subnets  we recommend: 1) deny-all NACL baseline; 2) allow only specific ports via SGs; 3) audit with flow logs and guardrails. also use AWS Network Firewall or third-party FW if you need application layer inspection.
[36:30] Mark: do you integrate with Palo Alto / Checkpoint?
[36:33] Jordan: we can peer with centralized inspection stacks or support inline inspection with a TGW firewall.

[38:20] Priya: on-prim considerations  we have an air-gapped environment for some models. can Redwood support on-prem or fully air-gapped deployment?
[38:32] Jordan: yes — we offer an on-prem package. for air-gapped we deliver a prepackaged bundle and a one-time model import workflow. operations are tooling-assisted but require local network controls; no outbound telemetry unless you opt in and provide a forwarder.
[39:00] Evan: how do upgrades work in air-gapped mode?
[39:05] Jordan: upgrades are staged via image bundles you import; Redwood provides signed artifacts and upgrade guides. optional assisted upgrade by our team under strict access windows.

[41:10] Maya: quick around objections  cost vs dedicated security: Evan?
[41:18] Evan: dedicated hosts increase cost but it's non-negotiable for compliance.
[41:22] Jordan: we can present cost delta and also a hybrid where certain sensitive workloads run on dedicated hosts and others on multi-tenant with strict isolation.

[44:00] Sofia: legal  data processing agreement / DPA?
[44:06] Maya: yes, we'll share standard DPA plus region-specific addenda. we'll also include a bridge letter for SOC2 time gaps.

[46:20] Jordan: operational runbooks: we provide playbooks for incident response, key compromise, and data deletion workflows. those are deliverables in the security pack.
[46:33] Priya: can we run a simulated incident to test the runbooks?
[46:37] Jordan: yes  tabletop exercises are supported. we can coordinate with your SRE on scenarios.

[49:00] Evan: latency concerns  we will do some perf-sensitive use-cases. how do you guarantee latency in private deployments?
[49:10] Jordan: dedicated capacity gives predictable latency; we also support pinned model instances and local KV caching. for additional guarantees we can configure pre-warmed nodes.

[51:30] Maya: returning to next steps  Jordan, what do you need from Latchford?
[51:38] Jordan: a staging account IAM role, CIDR ranges for routing, SSO metadata for SCIM/SAML, and a list of required data residency constraints. also the list of telemetry endpoints for egress rules.

[52:00] Evan: we'll send those by end of week.
[52:05] Priya: timeline  procurement is on a six-week runway; security review must be complete before procurement.
[52:12] Maya: understood, we'll prioritize SOC2 docs and the network checklist.

[54:00] Jordan: i'll also include a sample firewall rule-set and the one-page bench checklist.
[54:12] Mark: great.

[56:00] Sofia: one more legal: can Redwood support log redaction for PII?
[56:06] Jordan: yes, we provide configurable redaction rules and can run pre-send scrubbing for logs.

[58:00] Maya: recap: we will share SOC2/ISO artifacts, annotated architecture diagram, firewall checklist, and spin up a staging bench pending IAM. next call to review bench results.
[58:18] Evan: good summary.
[58:25] Priya: thanks everyone.
[59:00] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and security artifacts.
[60:00] (recording ends)
